options: A: full structural mirror in buildCompletedReadsSubsetCondition: provenance enum, book.title string, book.genres array of strings, pagesCount integer, authors array of {authorId uuid-shaped string, name string}, publisher null or {publisherId uuid-shaped, name string}, series null or the six typed fields; via jsonb_typeof and jsonb_path_exists

B: only the shapes current writers can actually produce wrong (genres null from the nullable books.genres column through the backfill migration, non-RFC UUIDs from explicit-id inserts), record the rest as RISK
C: no patch; record RISK_UNVERIFIED with the T13 evidence and a separate proposal, since no app code path writes such snapshots
openDecisions.codebaseCost: A is one SQL helper of about 20 predicates, no migration, no schema change; B is 2-4 predicates; C is zero code. The UUID check in SQL must copy the Zod 4.4.3 regex (node_modules/.pnpm/zod@4.4.3/node_modules/zod/v4/core/regexes.js:24), which is a second source of truth.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. The invariant row.completedReadCount === totalCount is the stated contract (reading-statistics-intervals.ts:166-170 describe text) and B leaves it conditional on data history. Keep it DB-side in the one helper and add a lockstep test that enumerates every schema field.
openDecisions.answer: A, conditional on T13 going red
openDecisions.decidedBy: main loop under the spec rule "phases run without approvals" (§9)
openDecisions.rationale: row.completedReadCount === totalCount is the published contract; a partial mirror keeps it conditional on data history. One helper, no migration, no schema change; the copied UUID regex is pinned by a parity test case.

openDecisions.question: Should Back/Forward step through period changes?
options: A: keep as is: tab/section push (use-statistics-view.ts:41), period setters use the nuqs default history (use-statistics-params.ts:45, no option)
B: pass { history: 'push' } to the period setters
openDecisions.codebaseCost: B is a one-line option, but spec §5 forbids rewriting URL parsers and §3 lists Back/Forward as already working
openDecisions.recommendation: A, record as PASS for tab/section/calendar history with a note that period changes do not create history entries
openDecisions.rationale: §5 forbids rewriting URL parsers and §3 counts Back/Forward as working; recorded as a note in S03.

openDecisions.question: The measured hotspot is countPriorExposure (245-320 ms of 290-420 ms, JIT triggered by a 2.59M-row estimate), not the bucket functions (<3%). Fix it in stage 04 or route it to a separate optimization package?
options: A: stage 04: rewrite countPriorExposure (statistics-completion.repository.ts:99-130) so authors and genres are not cross-joined per cycle (separate subqueries / unions), proving before/after time and byte-identical payloads
B: stage 04: disable JIT for that query (SET LOCAL jit = off inside a transaction)
C: DEFERRED: record the measurement and propose a separate package
openDecisions.codebaseCost: A touches one repository method plus a parity test; B needs a transaction around one raw query and is a session-setting change; C costs nothing now
openDecisions.recommendation: C. Spec §7.2 limits stage 04 changes to the bucket functions and §11 names a separate, measured optimization package as the next step; the measurement already gives that package its evidence. If the user wants it now, A over B, because A removes the misestimate instead of hiding it.
openDecisions.rationale: §1.4 allows changing a confirmed getOverview bottleneck with proof of gain and stable contract results; §7.4 bans only endpoint splits, Redis, tables, indexes and caches, none of which this touches. Measured on booknest_dev (synthetic user, 240 eligible cycles): original 400.6 ms with JIT (cost 1,801,804), rewrite with three scalar subqueries over one CTE 1.7 ms, cost 5,222, no JIT, identical author/genre/publisher arrays. Prod runs the same postgres:17-alpine image with default JIT thresholds (deploy/docker-compose.yml:32); prod JIT setting itself NOT_VERIFIED (no server access).

snapshotParity.conclusion: overview count <= subset totalCount for every row; the reverse cannot happen, because every snapshot that passes ReadingCompletionSnapshotSchema also passes every SQL predicate.
